column1: # GOOGLE PLAY LAUNCH CHECKLIST - Cat Metro (com.catmetro.game)
column2: personal Play developer account
column3: solo dev. Locked to DECISIONS_BRIEF 2026-07-31. Public 1.0 target Aug 24-28 2026 best case (planning basis P50 Sep 1-2 / P80 Sep 12-16); production submission the day access is granted (submit-on-grant; P50 ~Aug 20-21); Shipaton submission freeze Sep 26-30. All deadlines below are INTERNAL dates set ahead of Play's own statutory dates so the 3-5 week time-to-store (verified 2026-07-31) still lands inside the event window. Every row starts Not started; move to In progress / Done / Blocked and paste the evidence link in the tracker. URLs quoted in DECISIONS_BRIEF were verified 2026-07-31; the remaining Play Help article IDs are canonical but MUST be click-confirmed during the Aug 1 Console pass and corrected in place if Google has renumbered them. Risk cross-ref: R-01 (production access)
column5: R-16 (judge access).

column5: evidence_required

column2: Register the personal Google Play developer account with the one-time $25 USD fee using the launch Google account. Personal (non-organisation) accounts are subject to the 12-tester / 14-day closed-testing rule - this is the account type the whole schedule assumes. Do not create an organisation account midstream; it resets verification.
column5: Console screenshot showing developer account ID and Active status; $25 payment receipt archived in /ops/play/

column2: Complete Play Console identity verification: legal name, physical address, phone and government ID upload. Verification must be Verified (not Pending) before an app can be published to production, and Google can take several days - filing on Aug 1 leaves buffer ahead of the Aug 15 production-access application.
column5: Console > Account details screenshot showing Verification status = Verified, with date

column1: Payments profile and merchant account verified
column2: Create the Google payments profile and link a merchant account so in-app products can be sold. Without a verified merchant account the 6 IAP SKUs cannot be activated and RevenueCat cannot validate purchases. Verified 2026-07-31: Play service fee is 10% on the first $1M plus a 5% billing fee = 15% effective for us - use 15% in every revenue model.
column5: Console > Payments profile screenshot showing status Approved; test that the Monetize > Products page is unlocked

column1: Device verification via Play Console mobile app
column2: Complete device verification for the new personal developer account using the Play Console mobile app on a PHYSICAL Android device BEFORE any track publish (including the Day-1 closed-track upload) - new personal accounts cannot publish submissions until this is done and it is invisible from the web Console (verified via support answer/14316361).
column5: Play Console mobile app screenshot showing the account's device verification complete, dated before the first closed-track publish

column2: Create the app: name Cat Metro, default language en-US, type Game, category Puzzle, free with in-app purchases. Package name com.catmetro.game is IMMUTABLE after the first upload - triple-check spelling against the Unity Player Settings applicationIdentifier and the RevenueCat Android app entry before the Day 1 upload.
column5: Console app dashboard screenshot showing package com.catmetro.game; Unity Player Settings screenshot with the identical identifier

column1: AAB format and Play App Signing enrolled
column2: Upload an Android App Bundle (APK uploads are not accepted for new apps). Enrol in Play App Signing on first upload: Google holds the app signing key, we hold the upload key. Build config: IL2CPP, ARM64 only, targetSdk 36, minSdk 25, release build minified with R8 plus keep rules for Play Billing, Google Mobile Ads and OneSignal receivers. Back up the upload keystore and its passwords to two offline locations on Day 1 - a lost upload key costs days of support tickets mid-window.
column5: Console > App integrity screenshot showing Play App Signing enabled and both certificate SHA-256 fingerprints; encrypted keystore backup verified restorable on a second machine

column1: Closed testing: 12 testers for 14 continuous days
column2: Personal accounts must run a closed test with at least 12 testers who OPT IN and remain opted in continuously for 14 days before production access can be requested (verified 2026-07-31). Create the closed track and upload the first AAB on Aug 1 so the clock starts Day 1; recruit 18-20 testers, 12 minimum maintained through GRANT; check the opted-in headcount daily - the 14-day requirement is per-tester and trailing, so a dropout's days never accumulate and a drop below 12 on any day risks restarting the clock. Collect real qualitative feedback: the production-access form asks what was learned and generic answers get rejected.
column5: Daily screenshots of Console > Testing > Closed testing showing >=12 opted-in testers for each of Aug 1-15; the feedback log with at least 12 named testers and their written comments

column2: File the production-access application the same day the 14-day closed-testing clock completes. Answer with concrete specifics: what testers said, what changed as a result, target audience, monetisation model. Review is typically <=7 days, then the first production release gets its own review of up to 7 days - both must fit before the Aug 24-28 launch window. If rejected, address the stated reason and refile within 24 hours (R-01).
column5: Submitted application screenshot with timestamp; the full answer text archived; Console notification of the decision

column1: Daily email and spam monitoring during review windows
column2: Reviewer questions and forms are sometimes sent by email (occasionally landing in spam) and never appear in the Console. Check the developer-account inbox AND spam folder every day during both review windows - the production-access application review and the first-release review - and answer any reviewer email the same day (R-01).
column5: Daily monitoring log covering both review windows; any reviewer email and its same-day reply archived

column2: New apps and updates must target API 36 (Android 16) from Aug 31 2026, with an extension possible to Nov 1 2026 (verified 2026-07-31). Set targetSdkVersion 36 in Unity Player Settings from the first build - do not treat this as a launch-week task. Verify the manifest merger did not downgrade it and that no plugin (EDM4U-pulled AndroidX, Google Mobile Ads 11.3.0, OneSignal 5.3.2) forces a lower target.
column5: bundletool or aapt2 dump badging output from the release AAB showing targetSdkVersion=36; Console upload accepted with no target-API warning

column2: Billing Library 8+ is required from Aug 31 2026 (verified 2026-07-31). We satisfy this transitively: purchases-unity 9.7.0 ships Play Billing 8.3.0. Do NOT install Unity IAP - it pulls a second BillingClient and produces duplicate-class build failures (R-03). Verify the resolved Billing version in the EDM4U resolved-dependencies file and again in the AAB dependency list after every SDK change.
column5: EDM4U resolved dependencies file showing com.android.billingclient:billing 8.3.0 and exactly one entry; Console upload with no Billing deprecation warning; a real sandbox purchase of cm_all_access completing on the mid-tier device

column2: Create and activate all 6 products with the exact IDs and US prices: cm_all_access $6.99 (non-consumable, entitlement all_access), cm_supporter_pack $9.99 (non-consumable, supporter + all_access), cm_theme_sakura $2.99 and cm_theme_neon $2.99 (non-consumable), cm_rewind_5 $1.99 and cm_rewind_20 $4.99 (consumable). Use Play price templates for regional conversion, keep .99 endings, and mirror every ID exactly into RevenueCat products, entitlements and offerings. IDs are permanent - a typo means a dead SKU.
column5: Console > Products screenshot showing 6 Active products with matching IDs and prices; RevenueCat dashboard screenshot showing the same 6 products attached to the 4 entitlements; one sandbox purchase per SKU logged

column2: 16 KB page size is mandatory for apps targeting API 35+ (in force since Nov 2025, verified 2026-07-31). Audit every packaged .so - libil2cpp, libunity, libmain, Google Mobile Ads 11.3.0 natives, OneSignal 5.3.2 natives and anything EDM4U 1.2.188 resolves. Run the dedicated 16 KB emulator row of the device matrix at D14 and after every SDK or Unity change (R-14). Unity 6000.3.16f1 IL2CPP/ARM64 emits aligned output, but third-party libs are the real risk.
column5: zipalign -c -P 16 -v output exiting 0 with no BAD lines, archived per build; logcat from the 16 KB emulator showing a clean boot to Home with no UnsatisfiedLinkError; Console pre-launch report with no 16 KB warning

column2: Complete the Data safety declaration covering every SDK we ship. Collected/shared data across AdMob, OneSignal, RevenueCat and Firebase Crashlytics: approximate location, device and other IDs (advertising ID), purchase history, app interactions, crash logs, diagnostics. Declare data-in-transit encryption, our no-account-deletion rationale, and that no data is used for the prohibited purposes. Answers must match what the app actually does - a mismatch is a policy violation, not a paperwork error.
column5: Console > App content > Data safety screenshot showing Completed plus the exported answer summary archived; a line-by-line mapping sheet from each declared data type to the SDK that collects it

column2: Transcribe AdMob's published Play data-disclosure guidance into our form: advertising ID / device or other IDs (collected and shared, for advertising and analytics), approximate location, app interactions, and diagnostics. We serve rewarded ads only (no interstitials, banners or app-open ads), so declare the rewarded-ad data flows and nothing more.
column5: Screenshot of the AdMob disclosure page section used, annotated with each row copied into our form; our form rows highlighted for AdMob

column2: Declare OneSignal 5.3.2 data handling: device and other IDs (push token, OneSignal player ID), app interactions and custom events, tags, and the external_id we set via Login(). No email or phone collected. Confirm against OneSignal's personal-data documentation before submitting, and keep the tag list in sync with data/notification_copy.csv and data/onesignal_journeys.csv.
column5: Annotated OneSignal documentation section; the exact tag and custom-event list we send, exported from the analytics wrapper, matched against the declared data types

column2: Declare RevenueCat (purchases-unity 9.7.0) data handling: purchase history, app-user ID / device identifiers, and subscriber attributes we set ($onesignalUserId plus cohort labels). RevenueCat is a processor for purchase validation - declare it as collected for App functionality and Analytics, shared with a third party for purchase validation. Verify against RevenueCat's Play Data Safety documentation page (confirm the URL resolves; RevenueCat has reorganised its docs tree before).
column5: Annotated RevenueCat data-safety documentation page; the list of subscriber attributes we actually set, exported from CatMetro.Integrations.RevenueCat, matched to declared rows

column2: Declare Firebase Crashlytics: crash logs, diagnostics, device and other IDs, collected for App functionality and Diagnostics, not shared for advertising. Crash-free-rate evidence is also part of the Shipaton submission, so Crashlytics stays in the build - declare it properly rather than dropping it. Follow the Firebase Play data-disclosure guidance verbatim.
column5: Annotated Firebase data-disclosure page; Crashlytics dashboard screenshot showing the app reporting; our declared diagnostics rows

column2: Publish a privacy policy at https://catmetro.com/privacy covering AdMob, OneSignal, RevenueCat and Crashlytics, the advertising ID, children's-data position (13+, not Families), data retention, and the support contact. The URL must be live, publicly reachable without a login, and identical in the store listing and in-app Settings. Register catmetro.com on Aug 1 (RDAP-clean as of 2026-07-31) so the page exists well before the Data safety form is filed.
column5: Live URL returning 200 from a clean browser session; Console store-listing field populated with the same URL; in-app Settings link tested on device

column2: Declare Contains ads = Yes (we serve rewarded AdMob ads) and add the AD_ID permission declaration in the manifest plus the App content > Advertising ID section. Our ads are rewarded/opt-in only - no interstitials, banners or app-open ads at launch - and cm_all_access removes all non-rewarded ad surfaces permanently, which must be described accurately on the store listing. The Contains ads badge appears publicly, so the listing copy must set the expectation ('ads only when you ask for them').
column5: Console > App content > Ads screenshot showing the declaration; manifest excerpt showing com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID; store-listing copy referencing rewarded-only ads

column2: Publish app-ads.txt at https://catmetro.com/app-ads.txt containing the AdMob publisher line, and set the developer website in the Play listing to catmetro.com so the crawler can find it. Unauthorised-inventory status suppresses demand and depresses eCPM on a brand-new AdMob account (R-07). Confirm AdMob shows Authorised before the commercial beta on Aug 21.
column5: Live app-ads.txt returning 200; AdMob > App settings screenshot showing app-ads.txt status Authorised; Play listing website field set to catmetro.com

column2: Complete the IARC questionnaire honestly: no violence, no user-generated content, no user-to-user communication, no gambling or simulated gambling, digital purchases = Yes, rewarded ads present = Yes. Expected outcome ESRB Everyone / PEGI 3 with an in-app-purchases descriptor. Any listing change that alters the answers (e.g. adding leaderboards or chat) requires re-running the questionnaire.
column5: Console > App content > Content ratings screenshot showing the issued certificate and per-region ratings; the emailed IARC certificate archived

column1: Target audience 13+ and no child-appealing art
column2: Set target age groups to 13+ ONLY. Do not select any under-13 group - that pulls the app into the Families programme with its policy, ads-SDK and design requirements we are not built for. Play can also reject a listing whose art reads as child-directed even when 13+ is declared, so the icon, feature graphic and screenshots must show the premium tabletop-diorama look, not a cartoon-toy look (verified 2026-07-31). Have a second pair of eyes review the assets against this bar before upload.
column5: Console > App content > Target audience screenshot showing 13+ only and Appeal to children = No; the reviewed asset set with the reviewer's sign-off note

column2: Cat Metro creates no user accounts: no sign-in, no server profile, all progress is local with a client-side ticket and rewind ledger; RevenueCat uses an anonymous app-user ID and OneSignal a device push token. Declare 'app does not offer account creation' and keep a written rationale plus an in-app data-reset control (Settings > Reset progress, which clears local save, RC anonymous ID and OneSignal tags) as good-faith evidence. If any future build adds sign-in, this row becomes a blocking web-form requirement.
column5: Console > App content > Data deletion screenshot showing the no-account-creation declaration; written rationale archived; on-device demo of Settings > Reset progress recorded

column2: If the in-app review prompt ships, it must follow Google's rules: no visible CTA or button that triggers it, never shown after a failure or in exchange for a reward, and the quota is limited so requests may silently no-op. Our trigger: after a level WIN on a completed district, at most once per 30 days, never in the same session as a paywall or ad. Never assume the flow appeared - do not branch UI on the callback.
column5: Code review note pointing at the single call site with its guard conditions; device test showing no crash or UI stall when the quota suppresses the dialog; analytics event confirming the trigger fires at most once per 30 days

column2: Android 13+ (API 33+) requires runtime POST_NOTIFICATIONS consent before OneSignal can deliver push. Do not request it at first launch - request after the first Daily Line unlock (post L7) with a plain-language pre-prompt explaining the streak reminder. A denied permission must degrade cleanly: the app falls back to Unity Mobile Notifications local scheduling where possible and never blocks any gameplay.
column5: Device recording of the pre-prompt then system dialog on an API 33+ device; test evidence that a denial leaves the app fully playable; OneSignal dashboard showing subscription state changes

column2: Prepare and upload: app icon 512x512 32-bit PNG; feature graphic 1024x500; 2-8 phone screenshots, PNG or JPEG, 16:9 to 9:16, 320-3840 px per side (ours 1080x1920); 7in and 10in tablet screenshots; optional 30s-2min YouTube preview. Short description <=80 chars, full description <=4000 chars, both stating 'no forced ads' plainly. Keep the Shipaton submission assets (1024x1024 icon, 1179x2556 frameless screenshot) in the same export batch. No third-party trademarks or music anywhere.
column5: Asset manifest listing each file with its measured dimensions and byte size; Console store-listing preview screenshot; copy proofread and character counts recorded

column2: Every closed-track upload generates a pre-launch report (crawler runs on real Firebase Test Lab devices). Review stability, performance, accessibility and policy sections on every build from Aug 1, not just at launch. Treat any native crash on an API 35+ device as a 16 KB regression until proven otherwise (R-14). Accessibility findings about tap-target size must be fixed, not dismissed - our locked design bar is >=48dp.
column5: Pre-launch report screenshots for the release-candidate build showing zero crashes and zero ANRs across the crawler device set; a written disposition for every remaining warning

column2: SUBMIT-ON-GRANT rule: submit the first production release the DAY production access is granted (P50 ~Aug 20-21), using the current commercial-beta build, with managed publishing ON so the approved build is held until we press Publish; the polished 1.0 ships as an immediate update. Launch Aug 24-28 is the best case; planning basis P50 Sep 1-2, P80 Sep 12-16. Managed publishing decouples an unpredictable review finish from the launch date and lets the BuildInPublic announcement, promo codes and store-listing copy land on the same day. Turn it off (or publish immediately) only once the launch-day checklist is green.
column5: Console > Publishing overview screenshot showing Managed publishing = On before the release is submitted; the launch-day go/no-go checklist with timestamps

column2: The Shipaton rules require the app to be accessible from the USA (verified 2026-07-31). Set country availability to include the US from the very first production release and verify the US is present after every release edit - judges cannot evaluate what they cannot install (R-16). Ship broad availability rather than a staged country rollout; there is no time to widen it later.
column5: Console > Countries / regions screenshot with United States = Available; a US Play Store URL check (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.catmetro.game&gl=US) returning the live listing

column2: The EU Digital Services Act requires every developer distributing in the EU to declare trader status and, if a trader, publish contact and trader details. MANUAL VERIFY IN CONSOLE on Aug 1: the exact wording, the required fields and the help-article ID have all changed since introduction, so do not rely on this row's text - open Console > Account details / App content and complete whatever the current form asks. An undeclared or unverified trader status can block EU distribution entirely, which would shrink reach during the window.
column5: Console screenshot of the completed trader-status declaration with the verification state visible; a note recording the exact Console path and help-article ID found on the day, replacing this row's URL if it differs

column2: Google handles Play refunds; developers can also refund an order from Console within the allowed window. Publish a support email (support@catmetro.com) and the website in the store listing, and state the refund route in the in-app Settings > Help screen. Track refund rate as a monetisation-trust signal: >3% of orders is the R-12 tripwire that triggers a positioning review, not just a support reply. Target: respond to every store review or support email within 48 hours during the window.
column5: Live support@catmetro.com mailbox receiving a test message; Console listing screenshot showing the contact email and website; the Console refunds page bookmarked with the process written into the ops runbook

column1: In-app Promotions integrated in the app
column2: Play promo codes for one-time in-app products only work if the APP integrates In-app Promotions and the promoted buy option is Active (answer/6321495) - this is an app-side integration, not a dashboard-only task. Whether purchases-unity coexists cleanly with the In-app Promotions redemption flow is UNVERIFIED: prove it with an end-to-end promo-code redemption test on a clean device as an acceptance criterion at D17 (commerce build) and again at D24 (pre-submit sweep). If redemption fails, the judge-access mechanism named in the rules is broken (R-16) and fixing it becomes the top P0. Tracked as backlog issue CM-050.
column5: A recorded clean-device redemption of a test code showing the all_access entitlement arriving via CustomerInfo sync, captured at D17 and re-run at D24; CM-050 closed with both recordings attached

column2: After 1.0 is live, mint the launch batch of 25 one-time promo codes for cm_all_access: 15 reserved for Shipaton judges, 5 press, 5 spare (Play one-time codes verified 2026-07-31 to work for one-time in-app products; quarterly quota - reverify in Console before generating). Redeem-test 2 codes on a factory-reset device to prove the flow end to end, then include the judge codes plus a step-by-step redemption guide in the Devpost submission. Codes must be created after the product is Active and the app is published, so this is a post-launch, pre-submission task (R-16).
column5: Console promo-code batch screenshot showing 25 codes (15 judges / 5 press / 5 spare) with expiry dates; a recorded redemption on a clean device showing the all_access entitlement becoming active in RevenueCat; the redemption guide text drafted for Devpost

column2: Clear every other App content section so the release is not held: App access = no login required, all content reachable without credentials (state this explicitly for reviewers); News app = No; Health apps = No; Financial features = None; Government apps = No; Data safety refreshed after any SDK change. Play blocks the production release while ANY App content section is incomplete, so walk the full list top to bottom the same day the Data safety form is filed rather than discovering a missing section on launch day.
column5: Console > App content screenshot showing every section marked Completed with no outstanding warnings; a dated walkthrough note listing each section and its answer
